questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was important for me to go on exchange because I like to travel and I think that university-exchange is a unique possibility to try out how it is to have a daily life in another country. It was more or less incidientelly that Milan became my study destinationen since I had to choose between the remaining spots (restpladser). Nevertheless I chose Milan because I thought it could be nice to explore an European country and because I was curious about the Italian culture. Also the food and the weather was attractive.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I am grateful that I had the opportunity to study in Milan. The semester has been the most exciting and interesting semester. Milan as a study destination is highly recommended.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I don't remember this process as a big thing, but I'm not a big planner either. We were also a group from Denmark, so we shared information and helped each other. There was a bit confusing about what courses you could choose on the specific semester. It is an advantage if you are a bit proactive - I had two 3-point courses which I only found out was available because I wrote to the professors.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not much, so in the beginning it could be a little confusing to find the right classrooms. But I think the ones who arrived to Milan earlier than me had a tour at the University.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: If you are in doubt, reach out to the University or the other students and they will help you.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Unfortunately it is difficult and expensive to find housing in Milan. I stayed at Aparto Giovenale - a new dorm for international students. Aparto have a lot of rooms, so it was not difficult at all to get a room - just very expensive for a dorm. I don't know if I can recommend Aparto since there is a lot of ''special'' rules - for instance it is not allowed to have guests over after 19:00. But the location it great.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Don't really know.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I haven't heard that many good things about living in the accommodation offered by the university - only that it should be very cheap. So I don't regret living off-campus.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It's is very flexible - you can just keep on changing courses if you like.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I wrote to Massimo Costa, if I was in doubt of anything.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted. It doesn't seem like the professors reject anyone from taking a class, if you just ask them nicely.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is not a problem to get the courses you like. The thing that can be difficult is to take courses which don't overlap and to make up a good daily schedule.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Lower level than UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Some professors will include the students more in the lessons.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: An introduction to italian private law in a comparative perspective. Comparative contract law. EU law on business and human rights. European labour law. Fundamental rights in the European Union. Constitutional challenges in the EU.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Can recommend all of them. The professor in comparative contract law (Marchetti Carlo) was very good.

What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Rent and the supermarket was more expensive than expected - it is not cheaper than copenhagen. Wine, coffee, eating out and train tickets were cheap.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were some e-rasmus events.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Explore the citylife in Milan. Make some new friends. Try diffrent restaurants. Go for aperitivo. Jump on the train. Exercise. Read books. Learn the basic italian language.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Varenna (Como-lake), Sirmione (Garda-lake), Bologna, Venice, Florence, Umbria, Cinque Terre.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The italian lifestyle is laid-back and they take their time. This also means that some things can be slowly and events sometimes changes in the last minute. For me it was easy to adjust to the local culture. I think it depends on how much you like to plan your time ahead.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Choose some courses where they are. The courses I took was almost only exchange students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Sometimes the communication can be a little aggressive.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The people, the food, the humor, the good vibes.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: There is a lot of diffrent ways to go on an exchange - do what you like and enjoy. Milan is a great city.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not more than I already wrote and most of the things you will find out by yourself in time.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To make new friends. To learn the italian culture. To stay in the center of Europe and be close to a lot of beautiful places. To improve my English skills.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Missing my friends and boyfriend at home.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
